_comment: AI-generated scouting reports keyed by teamId. Structured data — rendered to HTML by the app. Photos come from player_photos.json (players without a photo get the silhouette). Empty object = use rules-based fallback.

hoover.summaryNote: Hoover is the second-ranked team in the league and the deepest lineup top-to-bottom. Every spot in the order is a threat — there are no easy outs. They score in bunches: expect multi-run innings and pressure on every pitch. Their lone loss was to undefeated St. Catherines.

lineup.tip: Elite table-setter. 17-for-19 on the season — the best pure hitter in the league. Gets on base at will and scores in nearly every game. 1 HR and high ISO — OF plays deep.
lineup.pitchTip: Keep it low — his power numbers demand you avoid belt-high pitches. No meatballs.

lineup.tip: Consistent run-producer with 12 runs scored. Has gap power and hit a solo HR vs St. Catherines. His extra-base hits suggest balls getting into the gaps — OF plays deep and shades the alleys.
lineup.pitchTip: Has home run power — keep it low and off the fat part of the plate.

lineup.tip: Cleanup-caliber bat hitting 3rd. 18-for-21 with 5 doubles and 10 RBI — the best gap hitter on the team. 5 doubles means balls are consistently getting into the gaps. OF plays deep and shades both alleys.
lineup.pitchTip: 5 doubles this season — don't give him anything easy to drive. Keep pitches low to limit extra-base damage.

lineup.tip: The most dangerous bat in the lower order. Team-high 14 RBI with a HR, triple, and 2 doubles. His mix of deep power and gap hits means OF needs to play deep and be ready in both alleys.
lineup.pitchTip: Highest ISO on the team (.438) — keep it low and don't give him anything to drive. With runners on, there are no free pitches.

lineup.tip: Has extra-base pop and a high-contact approach. His 4-for-4, 3-RBI game vs Washington showed he can take over an inning. A triple on his resume — OF plays deep.
lineup.pitchTip: Has a triple and a .917 SLG — keep pitches low to reduce extra-base contact.

lineup.tip: Solid contact hitter in the middle of the order. No extra-base hits — OF can play shallower when he's up.
lineup.pitchTip: Limited sample but solid contact rate — don't groove pitches. Make him earn it.

lineup.tip: The most-played player on the roster (6 games) with 11 RBI. Average has dipped recently. 2 doubles suggest occasional gap contact — OF plays standard depth, shading slightly toward the alleys.
lineup.pitchTip: Average has dipped recently but still has 11 RBI — don't get careless with runners on base.

lineup.tip: One of the more neutral bats in the lineup. No extra-base hits — OF can play shallower, focus on limiting his singles from becoming RBI opportunities.
lineup.pitchTip: Lowest AVG in the lineup (.364) — one of the more manageable outs. Don't walk him.

lineup.tip: High-contact 9-hole hitter with 10 runs scored — acts as a second leadoff spot. No extra-base hits, so OF can play shallower when he's up. Getting him out is key to breaking the rally cycle.
lineup.pitchTip: High contact rate, no extra-base hits — pitch carefully to avoid putting him on base as a table-setter.

lineup.tip: Reliable contact hitter in the 10-spot. No extra-base hits over 4 games — OF can play shallower. Focus on keeping him off base to prevent cycling back to the top of the order.
lineup.pitchTip: No extra-base hits this season — pitch to contact and let the defense work.

hoover.lineupNote: Batting order based on average lineup position across all games this season. Hoover regularly dresses 10+ players — Bryan Dow, Paul Dilaura, Brad Null, and Adam Ramirez are all capable of slotting in anywhere from 4-8 depending on game-day availability.

players.tip: The best bat in the league. ISO .421, 1 HR — keep pitches low, no meatballs. Play OF deep.
Team leader in RBI (14), ISO .438 — his power numbers are real. Keep it low, no easy pitches, especially with runners on.
Best gap hitter on the team. Pitch up & in — don't let him extend on the outer half.
Also a triples threat — shade gaps, play deep.
Avoid high & outside — he'll slap it to right field. Pitch low & in.
Electric from gap to gap. Keep him off the outer half of the plate.
Hits for a high average with a triple. Avoid high & outside. Slots in anywhere from 4-7.
Incredible 8-for-9 in limited games. Pure contact hitter — pitch down & keep it on the corners.
Small sample but consistent contact. Gets on base and contributes runs.
Drives in more than one run per hit. Consistently comes through with runners on base — his extra-base hits are likely reaching the gaps or going deep.
Matches Dow's RBI rate despite being a contact-only hitter (.500 AVG, no XBH). Excels at driving in runs with singles — don't let him bat with runners on.
Converts hits to RBI at a 1:1 rate over 6 games. Most experienced player on the roster — reliable in run-scoring situations.
High RBI total is driven by pure volume — he's on base so often that his own RBI numbers accumulate even as others score him.

sections.title: Table Setters (score more than they drive in)

players.tip: Scores runs at a dramatically higher rate than he produces them — he gets on base and the big bats bring him in. Getting him out early disrupts the rally cycle.
Scores frequently but rarely drives in runs himself. A pure table-setter — focus on keeping him off base rather than pitching around him.
Nearly balanced, but scores slightly more than he drives in — plays both roles depending on lineup context.

gamePlan.heading: Play the OF deep across the board.
gamePlan.tip: 14 doubles and 3 HRs this season — extra-base hits suggest balls are regularly getting over or past outfielders. A shallow OF will give up runs.

gamePlan.heading: No free passes in the middle of the order.
gamePlan.tip: Seacrest, Koblis, and Dow all hit .750+ on the season. Every walk in the 1-4 spots essentially puts a run on base. Pitch to contact and trust your defense.

gamePlan.heading: Dow and Cohendet are your most dangerous RBI situations.
gamePlan.tip: Both have an RBI-per-hit ratio above 1.0, meaning they consistently drive in multiple runners per hit. Extra vigilance when they come up with runners on.

gamePlan.heading: Stepanian leads off the order a second time.
gamePlan.tip: He scores 3x more runs than he drives in (+7 R vs RBI), meaning he's consistently on base when the big bats come up. Getting him out quickly is key to breaking their rally cycle.

gamePlan.heading: Their only loss: Dow went quiet.
gamePlan.tip: In the 22-21 loss to St. Catherines, Dow went 2-for-3 with 0 RBI — well below his usual production. When Dow is neutralized, Hoover is beatable even in a high-scoring game.

franklin.summaryNote: Franklin is a contact-and-gaps team with the most triples in the league (7) and a .591 team AVG. They play tight games — two of their three losses were by a single run. They can be shorthanded at times, which shortens the lineup, but their top 4 bats are legitimate threats in any game.

lineup.tip: The best bat on the team. 14-for-17 with 8 doubles and a triple — his extra-base hit rate suggests balls consistently getting into the gaps or over outfielders. Sets the table for the entire lineup.
lineup.pitchTip: His 8 doubles are the most on the team — keep pitches low to limit gap contact. No easy pitches early in the game.

lineup.tip: Bats 2nd and drives in runs at exactly 1:1 per hit across 5 games. Consistently produces in RBI situations despite a modest average — a reliable middle-of-the-order threat from the leadoff area.
lineup.pitchTip: High RBI rate means he hits when it counts. Don't groove pitches with runners on base.

lineup.tip: 3 triples this season — tied for most in the league. High ISO (.529) and extra-base rate suggest he's consistently putting balls into the deep outfield. Gets on base via walks too (2 BB).
lineup.pitchTip: Keep it low — his triple count and ISO suggest balls are getting deep. Limiting his extra-base damage is key.

lineup.tip: The only player on the team with a home run, and the highest RBI-per-hit rate (1.12). His 5 extra-base hits across 5 games show consistent power. The most dangerous bat with runners on base.
lineup.pitchTip: Only HR on the team — keep it low. His RBI rate above 1.0 means he consistently drives in multiple runners per hit.

lineup.tip: The most consistent contact hitter in the lineup. .700 AVG over 5 games with no slumps — he is almost always on base. Rarely hits for extra bases but rarely makes outs.
lineup.pitchTip: High average, limited power (.800 SLG, ISO .100) — pitch to contact and let the defense work.

lineup.tip: Bats 7th but hits like a cleanup man in that slot. 1.00 RBI/H rate with 2 triples and 11 RBI — the most RBI on the team. His extra-base production from low in the order makes the entire bottom of the lineup dangerous.
lineup.pitchTip: Don't let the batting slot fool you — 11 RBI from the 7-hole is elite production. Keep it low with runners on.

lineup.tip: Hits for a high average with extra-base pop. 4 XBH in 4 games suggests consistent hard contact. Provides depth in the middle of the order when Rokovich or others are absent.
lineup.pitchTip: 4 extra-base hits in 4 games — keep it low, don't serve up anything easy to drive.

lineup.tip: Solid contact hitter in limited appearances. No extra-base hits — a singles hitter who stays out of the lineup on shorthanded days.
lineup.pitchTip: No extra-base power — pitch to contact and play the IF up.

lineup.tip: Consistent presence across all 5 games. No extra-base hits — OF can play shallower when he's up. Keeps innings alive with contact.
lineup.pitchTip: No extra-base hits this season — pitch to contact and trust the defense.

lineup.tip: In every game this season — a reliable presence at the bottom of the order. Scores more than he drives in (+3 R vs RBI), which means he gets on base and relies on the lineup behind him. 1 double, otherwise a singles hitter — OF plays standard depth.
lineup.pitchTip: 1 double in 5 games, otherwise no extra-base power. Pitch to contact.

lineup.tip: Bats at the bottom of the order but contributes a triple and 5 RBI. Takes walks (2 BB) — patient enough to work counts and get on base. A sneaky threat in the 10-hole.
lineup.pitchTip: Takes walks — don't nibble. Throw strikes and get ahead in the count.

franklin.lineupNote: Batting order based on average lineup position across all games. Franklin regularly dresses 11 players. When shorthanded, the top 4 (Lanam, Sosnick, Pierce, Rokovich) are almost always present and carry the offense.

players.tip: 3 triples is the most on the team and among the most in the league. Balls are consistently getting past or over outfielders. Play OF deep.
2 triples from the 7-hole. His extra-base production is well above average for his lineup position — don't shade the OF in when he's up.
2 triples and a HR — the most well-rounded power threat on the team. Keep it low.
The only HR on the team. ISO .450 is elite — his extra-base hits suggest real power, not just gap singles. Keep it low, no meatballs.
8 doubles in 4 games — the highest doubles total on the team by far. His ISO is even higher than Rokovich's, driven by volume gap contact. Play OF deep.
Team leader in RBI from the 7-hole. Consistently drives in runners — don't let him bat with runners on base without making him earn it.
Highest RBI-per-hit rate on the team. The most dangerous bat with the bases loaded.
Drives in runs at exactly 1:1 per hit. Consistent RBI production from the 2-spot despite a .500 average.
Scores and drives in at nearly the same rate — plays both roles. The engine at the top of the order.
Scores more than he drives in from the bottom of the order — a patient hitter (2 BB) who gets on base and lets the lineup cycle back around.
Scores more than he drives in — contributes by getting on base for the big bats ahead and behind him.

gamePlan.heading: Play the OF very deep — this is a triples-heavy lineup.
gamePlan.tip: Franklin has 7 triples this season, the most in the league. Extra-base hits suggest balls are regularly getting past outfielders. A shallow OF will give up extra bases on almost every hard contact.

gamePlan.heading: The top 4 are always in the lineup — the rest varies.
gamePlan.tip: Lanam, Sosnick, Pierce, and Rokovich appear in virtually every game. Focus your preparation on neutralizing this core — when Franklin is shorthanded, stopping these four is enough to win.

gamePlan.heading: Don't sleep on VanZandt in the 7-hole.
gamePlan.tip: 11 RBI from the 7-spot is the most on the team. He consistently drives in runners that the top of the order puts on base. Extra attention when he comes up with runners on.

gamePlan.heading: They play close games — one big inning can decide it.
gamePlan.tip: Two of their three losses were by a single run. Franklin doesn't blow out opponents or get blown out often. A multi-run inning, especially off their top pitchers, can be the difference.
